My first try saving some tomato seeds this year was about three weeks ago:

https://files.catbox.moe/8pmh6e.JPG

These did not want to come clean after a day or so of soaking. Then I spaced them for a few days and some of them were sprouting and I figured the whole batch decided to sprout so I planted the whole lot of them.

Update: The way I learned how to save tomato seeds was to let the last ones of the season ripen all the way until they dry on the vine and then crumble them to get the seeds. Always worked pretty good for my dad. Having read about this some everyone was saying that you only need let them ripen well and then put the seeds+gel in some water for a day or two and the gel would come off, at which point you wash them to get rid of as much of the gel as possible, and then dry the seeds and store. Well, it turns out the internet "experts" do not know as much about this as my dad, because soaking them to remove the gel has resulted in the seeds sprouting twice now. The second time they only soaked for 18 hours. At least half of these have tails coming out:

https://i.ibb.co/x6xPR7V/Mater-seeds-04.jpg

Good to know these seeds are viable, but the method of soaking tomato seeds for a day or two doesn't work if you plan on storing them. I guess I'll plant these ones and try to store the rest, but I have my doubts. They all might have already started to sprout, so when dried they will just die. I will try my dad's method when my plants give out, but between now and then I guess maybe I will try collecting some and just washing as much gel off without the recommended soak and then immediately dry them.
